event.description: Tie the rank-3 factorized positional segment code for the two reversed padded operand fields while retaining distinct BOS, separator, equals, output, and EOS segment codes, shared digit-index positions, learned expansion, shared no-offset normalization, d=14, h=2, L=2, ff=19, and the 45000-step schedule.
event.proposal: Family: position representation. Retained incumbent is attempt-0045 with 2980 parameters at 99.960000%, a +0.960000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the most recent accepted result is attempt-0045, 7 segment codes plus shared digit-index codes (2980, 99.96%); the most recent failed result is attempt-0036, reversed operands with rank-2 learned positions, an optimization failure peaking near 11.1% validation; 12 prior position-representation macro attempts plus a rank-7 schedule reattempt. Hypothesis: with inputs containing two identically formatted, reversed ten-digit operands, their learned role offsets need not differ once the plus token and causal order identify the fields. Mapping both operand spans to one segment code reduces the segment table from 7x3 to 6x3, lowering actual parameters from 2980 to 2977 while preserving digit-index alignment and the distinct output role. This is structured semantic parameter sharing within the accepted factorized positional representation, not scalar pruning. It is more informative than tying every delimiter code at once because it isolates the exchangeable operand-role assumption before changing boundary or output distinctions.
